title: Understanding Linear Models
text: A linear model is one where the relationship between the dependent variable and the independent variables is linear in the parameters. This means that the parameters (theta) are not multiplied together, raised to a power, or involved in any non-linear transformations.

title: Identifying Linear Models
text: Consider the structure of the equation. If the equation can be expressed as a linear combination of the parameters, it is a linear model. For example, $$y=\theta_1 x_1+\theta_2 x_2$$ is linear because it is a sum of terms, each of which is a parameter multiplied by a variable.
